overview: Markets: Sensex and Nifty fell for a fourth session as the rupee slipped and RBI's rate panel convened.
Big story: Ethiopian government forces advanced deep into Tigray as the rebel TPLF retreated toward full defeat.

items.headline: Russia strikes Kyiv bridges again as Germany's Merz visits Ukraine
items.summary: Russian forces hit a Kyiv bridge for the fourth straight day just as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived to meet President Zelenskyy. Kyiv says it will strike Russian refineries in response to Moscow's new doctrine of broader attacks on civilian infrastructure.

items.headline: Ethiopian forces advance in Tigray as rebels retreat
items.summary: Ethiopia's federal army pushed deeper into Tigray, encircling and entering the regional capital Mekelle as TPLF fighters withdrew. The advance marks the most dramatic shift yet in fighting that reignited in September, raising fears of a return to full-scale civil war.

items.headline: Houthis claim missile and drone strike on Saudi Aramco site
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis said they hit an Aramco facility in Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones, claiming retaliation for Saudi strikes on Sanaa. A Saudi-led coalition spokesman dismissed the claim as misleading, but witnesses reported smoke and fire near the site.

items.headline: Brazil's Lula and Bolsonaro head into tight election
items.summary: Brazilians voted in a deeply polarised presidential election pitting incumbent Lula against Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of the jailed former president. A runoff looms on October 25 if neither wins outright, in a race widely seen as a test of Trump's influence in Latin America.

items.headline: RBI's rate panel begins meeting as hike looms
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee began a three-day meeting, with economists expecting a 25-basis-point hike to 5.5% as inflation and global rate pressures build. The decision, due October 7, will shape borrowing costs across India's economy.

items.headline: South Africa hit by spate of deadly mass shootings
items.summary: A wave of gun attacks killed more than 46 people across South Africa in under a week, including 18 shot dead at a Carletonville tavern. The violence has alarmed officials just as the country had been making progress against its notoriously high murder rate.

items.headline: North Korea tests missile it says evades defenses
items.summary: Kim Jong Un oversaw a test of an intermediate-range missile that Pyongyang claims flew about 1,000 km, roughly 300 km further than Tokyo and Seoul had estimated, with manoeuvring capability designed to beat missile defences. The launch deepens tension after a recent DMZ land-mine incident.

items.headline: Taiwan presses Trump administration on stalled arms sale
items.summary: Taiwan's representative in Washington said he remains confident President Trump will approve a long-delayed $14 billion weapons package, even as the administration weighs the sale against its China relationship. Taiwan is separately set to receive its full order of Himars rocket systems this year.

items.headline: Philippine court clears path for Duterte impeachment trial
items.summary: The Philippine Supreme Court dismissed petitions challenging a lowered voting threshold for convicting Vice President Sara Duterte, clearing the way for her impeachment trial in the Senate to proceed. The ruling removes a key legal obstacle in one of the country's biggest political showdowns.

items.headline: Egypt hosts Horn of Africa security summit amid tensions
items.summary: Leaders of Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan met in Cairo and agreed to a regular mechanism for coordinating regional security, reaffirming support for each other's sovereignty. The summit comes as Ethiopia's renewed Tigray war unsettles its neighbours and strains regional ties.

items.headline: Israeli strike kills mother and daughter in Gaza
items.summary: An Israeli attack killed a mother and daughter in Gaza City, drawing mourning from the enclave's Christian community, as violations of the year-old ceasefire continue. Rights groups say well over a thousand Palestinians have been killed since the truce took effect.

items.headline: Explosions reported near Iran's Qeshm and Sirik islands
items.summary: Blasts were heard near Iran's Qeshm and Sirik islands amid simmering regional tensions, as President Pezeshkian said Tehran remains open to talks with Washington despite past strikes. The US is separately sending a third carrier strike group to the Middle East.

items.headline: Imran Khan's party marches on Islamabad demanding release
items.summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf pressed ahead with a long march toward Islamabad, with its Khyber Pakhtunkhwa unit weighing a prolonged stay in Swabi, to demand the release of jailed founder Imran Khan. The protest adds to pressure on Shehbaz Sharif's government.

items.headline: Magnitude 4.9 earthquake jolts Afghanistan
items.summary: An earthquake measuring magnitude 4.9 struck Afghanistan in the early hours of Monday, the latest tremor in a country prone to seismic activity along major fault lines. No immediate casualties or major damage were reported, though authorities continue assessing affected areas.

items.headline: Bangladesh open to regional bloc with Pakistan, minus India
items.summary: A senior Bangladeshi official said Dhaka could strategically join a new regional bloc alongside Pakistan that excludes India, unlike other South Asian states. The remarks follow friendlier recent meetings between Pakistan's PM Shehbaz Sharif and Bangladesh's interim leader Muhammad Yunus.

items.headline: Protests erupt in Delhi, Mumbai against Election Commission chief
items.summary: Demonstrators demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter-list manipulation clashed with police in Delhi and Mumbai, with roads barricaded and hundreds detained. The protests centre on the contentious Special Intensive Revision of voter rolls.

items.headline: Allahabad High Court bans hookah bars across Uttar Pradesh
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court ruled that hookah bars cannot operate anywhere in Uttar Pradesh, extending the ban even to designated smoking areas. The order tightens an already strict state crackdown on hookah venues that authorities say skirt tobacco-control rules.

items.headline: Allahabad court blocks custody switch to protect girl's schooling
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court set aside an order shifting custody of a 10-year-old girl to her father, ruling that courts must first examine whether her education can continue uninterrupted with her mother. The girl had told the court she wished to stay with her mother.

items.headline: Madras High Court orders safety rules for temple elephants
items.summary: The Madras High Court directed Tamil Nadu to frame a standard operating procedure regulating captive elephants used at temple festivals, mandating regular health and safety checks. The order follows long-running concerns over the welfare of elephants paraded at religious events.

items.headline: Delhi court: bank transfers alone can't set alimony
items.summary: The Delhi High Court ruled that bank transactions alone cannot be treated as a husband's monthly disposable income when determining maintenance payments. The judgment adds nuance to how courts assess a spouse's true earning capacity in matrimonial disputes.

items.headline: Rajasthan court grants back wages to acquitted employee
items.summary: The Rajasthan High Court held that an employee terminated by his employer after being acquitted in a criminal case is entitled to back wages until reinstatement. The ruling reinforces protections for workers cleared of charges that led to their dismissal.

items.headline: Delhi logs most polluted start to October in 4 years
items.summary: Delhi's air quality index worsened to its poorest start to October in four years, with PM2.5 and PM10 levels climbing as stubble burning and weak ventilation set in. The capital's AQI is forecast to stay in the moderate-to-poor range this week.

items.headline: Maharashtra postpones state services exam after student protests
items.summary: Maharashtra's Public Service Commission postponed its state services main examination for 2026 after student protests, and will review last year's answer sheets. The move follows pressure from aspirants demanding clarity on disputed questions and grading.

items.headline: Railways adds 162 special trains for Diwali, Chhath rush
items.summary: Indian Railways rolled out 162 additional special trains, part of a 580-train festive push, to handle the surge in travel to Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Delhi for Diwali and Chhath. New routes link Kanpur, Bengaluru, Varanasi and Ayodhya.

items.headline: Sensex, Nifty fall for fourth straight session
items.summary: The Sensex dropped 571 points to 71,909.70 and the Nifty fell 198 points to 22,421.95, extending a four-session losing streak as foreign investors sold, the rupee weakened and global bond yields and crude prices climbed. The benchmarks have now lost over 2.5% in four sessions.

items.headline: India's forex reserves post biggest-ever weekly fall
items.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $18.3 billion to $747.6 billion in the week ended September 25, the sharpest weekly drop on record, as the RBI sold dollars to defend a weakening rupee. Foreign currency assets accounted for most of the decline.

items.headline: India's IPO market set for a record October
items.summary: India's IPO pipeline is on track for a record month, led by Jio Platforms' expected listing valuing it above Rs 12 trillion and Tata Capital's roughly $1.7 billion offering, the biggest since Hyundai's India debut. Strong domestic mutual-fund inflows are helping absorb the heavy new issuance.

items.headline: Indian startups draw fresh funding led by Simple Energy
items.summary: Electric two-wheeler maker Simple Energy raised Rs 1,750 crore in a Series C round, taking its total funding past Rs 2,530 crore, while AI chipmaker SiMa.ai closed a $150 million round backed by Fidelity and Dell Technologies Capital. Deeptech, EV and healthcare drew the heaviest investor interest this week.

items.headline: Drone maker ideaForge faces Rs 109-crore GST demand
items.summary: Tax authorities issued ideaForge a Rs 109.2-crore GST demand and penalty for alleged underpayment between January 2022 and March 2024, arguing the drone maker wrongly paid a lower 5% rate. The company plans to appeal, saying it expects no material near-term impact.

items.headline: OPEC+ holds oil output steady for a second month
items.summary: OPEC+ agreed to keep November production targets unchanged, extending a pause after six months of gradual increases, as Gulf exporters pump below quota amid Mideast supply disruptions. Brent crude held near $102 a barrel on the decision and regional security risks.

items.headline: Wall Street steadies as investors await Fed minutes
items.summary: US stock futures were little changed as investors weighed elevated Treasury yields and awaited the Federal Reserve's meeting minutes for clues on the path of rates. Soft jobs data had earlier cut the odds of an October rate move, lending some support to equities.

items.headline: Paramount-Warner Bros Discovery merger to be named Skydance
items.summary: Skydance chief David Ellison announced the combined Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery will operate under the Skydance name once their roughly $110 billion merger closes this week. The tie-up unites franchises including Mission Impossible, Harry Potter and the DC Universe under one studio.

items.headline: Senate Democrats press Big Tech on AI tax write-offs
items.summary: Senator Elizabeth Warren and other Senate Democrats sent letters to Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft demanding a breakdown of tax deductions claimed for AI hardware and data centres, giving the companies until mid-October to respond. The probe targets how the firms' tax bills have fallen amid the AI spending boom.

items.headline: Apple tightens macOS disk-access controls over AI agent risk
items.summary: Apple said it is tightening macOS's Full Disk Access permission, warning that increasingly capable AI agents make broad file and message access riskier. The move follows a claim that Meta's Muse app synced over 187,000 rows of a user's message history without clear consent.

items.headline: Pentagon breach exposes records of nearly 3 million people
items.summary: Hackers exploited a file-sharing vulnerability to access the Pentagon's personnel database undetected for roughly nine months, exposing names, Social Security numbers and service records of nearly three million current and deceased personnel. The intrusion was discovered only after the flaw was patched in July.

items.headline: Reddit to end RSS feeds and public API access
items.summary: Reddit will stop supporting RSS feeds in November and shut its public API by March 2027, citing abuse by AI scrapers, while keeping lucrative paid licensing deals with Google and OpenAI intact. The move will cut off third-party apps and research tools relying on open access.

items.headline: WHO: life expectancy nears pre-pandemic levels, cholera deaths surge
items.summary: A new WHO Global Health Estimates report found life expectancy has largely recovered to pre-pandemic levels, even as cholera deaths rose 30% in 2025 to 7,870, the highest since 1999. Total cholera cases fell, suggesting outbreaks are becoming deadlier even as they shrink in number.

items.headline: SpaceX's Crew-13 reaches ISS in under 8 hours
items.summary: A SpaceX Crew Dragon carrying NASA, Canadian and Russian astronauts docked with the International Space Station less than eight hours after launch, setting a new speed record for a US spacecraft. The crew includes NASA's Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney among others.

items.headline: Massive genome study finds bats originated in Europe
items.summary: An international Bat1K consortium study combining 103 bat genomes with 44 fossils found bats arose roughly 60 to 65 million years ago in Europe, overturning earlier theories of Asian, African or North American origins. The work also redrew the bat family tree and traced the evolution of echolocation and flight.

items.headline: India beat Pakistan to retain Asian Games cricket gold
items.summary: India defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in the Asian Games men's cricket final, completing a cricket double after the women's team also topped the podium. It capped a Games in which India swept gold across cricket, hockey, wrestling, archery and golf on the final day.

items.headline: India win back-to-back Asian Games hockey gold
items.summary: India beat Malaysia 5-1 to win the men's hockey gold for a second consecutive Asian Games, the first time the team has won back-to-back titles. India also claimed the women's hockey gold, sweeping both titles at the same Games for the first time.

items.headline: Aman Sehrawat leads India's wrestling sweep at Asian Games
items.summary: Aman Sehrawat won gold while Antim Panghal took silver and Deepak Punia claimed bronze as India added three more wrestling medals at the Asian Games. India finished the Games with 85 medals overall, including 21 gold, placing fourth in the final tally.

items.headline: Verstappen wins chaotic Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia
items.summary: Max Verstappen converted pole position into victory at a delay-marred Bahrain Grand Prix held in Malaysia, with Kimi Antonelli second to extend his championship lead. George Russell suffered a late engine failure, while Lewis Hamilton fought through the field to finish on the podium.

items.headline: Djokovic beats Zverev to reach China Open semis
items.summary: Novak Djokovic came from behind to beat Alexander Zverev 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 at the China Open, keeping alive his bid for a record-extending seventh Beijing title. The win sets up a semi-final test as the 38-year-old continues to chase late-career titles.

items.headline: Abdusattorov climbs to world No. 5 on FIDE list
items.summary: Nodirbek Abdusattorov rose two spots to world number five on October's FIDE rating list after a strong showing in Samarkand, while 15-year-old Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus became the highest-rated player of that age ever at world No. 17. Both stood out on an eventful ratings update.
